title: Pilot weekly ops, access, and environment snapshot
summary: Quick sync to review pilot onboarding progress, access handoffs, early benchmark anomalies, and plan fixes. Main blockers: KMS integration pending, VPC egress rules, and telemetry key rotation. Decided to run a small canary with dedicated pool and continue hosted fallback.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-12 15:00 PST | Duration 42m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Sarah, Ethan, Priya

Summary (auto): Maya: kickoff. quick status. Liam: bench numbers and triage. Sarah: infra constraints. Priya: sec checklist.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Okay everyone, thanks for joining, we got 42 minutes on the agenda, I'll kick off. Quick roll call? ->
[00:14] Sarah: Sarah here.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan, hi.
[00:18] Priya: Priya on info sec.
[00:20] Liam (SE): Liam from Redwood.
[00:22] Maya: Great. So goal today is a short snapshot of onboarding progress, outstanding access items, and the bench anomalies you flagged.

[02:05] Liam: Quick context — last week's synthetic run showed a 95th pct spike around the 2k token mark, looks like KV cache cold miss patterns and some tail lat on the smaller batch sizes. I dropped the raw CSV into the shared drive: https://redwood.app/pilot/auriga/bench-20270205.csv
[02:42] Ethan: yea we saw that with our burst tests, after 10k requests the latency moves. We are still on the hosted sandbox, but we want to try dedicated for the canary next week.

[06:10] Priya: security first — KMS integration is not finished, our key rotation policy needs to be applied and the HSM flow hasn't been validated. We're blocked on obtaining the customer-managed key ARN from Redwood's doc. The security pack link you sent is helpful but we need an AD/SSO flow demo.
[06:46] Maya: noted. I'll resend the KMS snippet and a short runbook. Also we can do a short SSO test with a temp account today if that helps.

[09:30] Sarah: access handoff status — Ethan has 2/3 egress rules in place, still waiting for the private subnet peering confirmation. Also the gateway token timed out once during bench.
[10:02] Ethan: that was my mistake — I rotated the gateway certs during the run, sorry for noise. We'll rerun after peering is confirmed.

[12:15] Liam: Bench detail — the tail is sensitive to sequence length and to quant configuration. We suspect the quant profile used was q4_0 but the model was on a q3b path; mismatch caused kernel fallback in runtime, which explains per-token lat spikes. There's also noise from continuous batching when requests are bursty.
[12:50] Sarah: can you explain kernel fallback? we don't want silent perf cliffs in prod.
[13:05] Liam: sure — essentially if the runtime can't use the optimized kernel for that data pattern, it falls back to a generic path, higher latency. We can pin quant profile per model to avoid that, or run a small shard on dedicated GPUs.

[16:40] Priya: from compliance, SOC2 artefacts look good; we need audit logs for access to health PII endpoints — can you enable field-level audit logs? Also KMS key custody proof.
[17:05] Maya: yes, we can enable detailed audit logs for the pilot. I'll share the link to the audit retention options: https://redwood.app/security/audit

[20:00] Ethan: networking note — VPC egress to redwood endpoints needs 3 IP ranges whitelisted, doc lists them but our firewall team requires a CIDR mapping. Can you provide a static ip range for the dedicated canary?
[20:26] Liam: For hosted we use region ranges; for Dedicated we can allocate a static NAT IP on request — takes 48-72 hours provisioning.

[23:33] Sarah: timeline — we want to validate canary in staging by Feb 19th, rollout to blue/green test by Feb 24th if canary passes. Is that realistic?
[23:50] Maya: yes, if we close KMS and peering by Feb 16th. Otherwise we'll push the canary a week.

[27:12] Liam: proposed mitigations for the bench: 1) pin quant profile; 2) enable prefix/KV caching for the prompt sets; 3) increase batch cap for the dedicated pool; 4) turn on trace sampling to capture kernel fallback traces.
[27:45] Ethan: can we toggle prefix caching at runtime or is that a restart?
[28:01] Liam: it's config driven, safe to flip but needs careful TTL settings — small cache ttl first.

[31:00] Priya: if we go dedicated, what about data residency? we require EU-only keys for some data flows.
[31:22] Maya: Dedicated can be confined to region; we can also opt for Private (VPC) deployment if strict data residency is required — that's a separate contract but available.

[34:10] Sarah: we also want a short run of adversarial prompt evals to check quality regressions after quant changes.
[34:33] Liam: good call — we'll run a 1k prompt eval and send the rerank metrics.

[37:05] Maya: recap: KMS ARN and runbook — Maya to send; peering confirmation — Ethan to complete; set up dedicated canary request — Maya+Liam; pin quant profile + small eval — Liam; audit logs enable — Maya. Can we agree owners and due dates?
[37:30] Priya: yes.

[38:10] Maya: ok final tidbits — I'll open a ticket in your workspace with the checklist and attach the bench CSV and a short 'how-to' for the KMS/HSM handshake. Also competitor note: you mentioned Anthropic internals — we won't discuss their stack but we can show comparative latency-cost in the next deck.
[38:45] Ethan: thanks all.
[39:00] Sarah: thanks, talk soon.
[39:12] Meeting end.
